title: Isaac del Toro extends UAE Team Emirates contract following Tour de France podium
content:
Isaac del Toro has extended his contract at UAE Team Emirates XRG through to 2031.

The 22-year-old’s previous deal had been set to expire in 2029 but he has committed his long-term future to the team just two weeks after his third-place finish in the Tour de France.

Del Toro’s podium placement came after his first Tour stage win, aided to the line by leader and race-winner Tadej Pogacar, and secured the white jersey ahead of French prodigy Paul Seixas.

The stage 2 win on Montjuic followed a successful season for the Mexican, after victories at the UAE Tour, Tirreno-Adriatico and Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes (previously the Criterium du Dauphiné).

“This team feels like home,” Del Toro said in a release on Thursday. “We share the same ambition, the same passion for racing and the same desire to keep getting better.

“Signing long-term gives me a lot of confidence because I know I’m in the right place for my future.

“We’ve already achieved some amazing victories together, but I honestly believe the best is still to come. I’m excited to keep growing with this team and fighting for the biggest races in the world.”

Del Toro joined UAE in 2024. Last season he finished second in the Giro d’Italia and won the white jersey, after ceding his lead to Simon Yates on the Colle delle Finestre.

Securing Del Toro’s future is a huge win for UAE.

He has developed into a serious GC contender in his own right, and would walk into most World Tour teams as their leader.

As such, transfer rumours had swirled around a potential move away to occupy that role, instead of domestiqueing under the inevitable Pogacar, who won a record-equalling Tour de France this summer.

De Toro seemed to build an incredibly strong bond with the 27-year-old Slovenian over the French grand tour, however, as the world champion marshalled him to his first Tour stage win. Even towards the end of the race, Pogacar flipped the hierarchy and rode for Del Toro in stage 20, with his own GC win wrapped up.

For the rest of the peloton, this is a scary sight. The one-two of the pair is incredibly strong and is nearly impossible to beat.

Would it have been more exciting if he moved to take the No 1 spot elsewhere? Yes. But Pogacar, who himself is on a contract until 2030, clearly sees Del Toro as something of a successor, and in that sense the writing was on the wall.
